title: Moving the sofa
topic: A friend estimates when movers carrying a sofa up the stairs will reach the 8th floor
blurb: They hit the 4th floor in 6 minutes, so the 8th floor should be another 6 — right?
prompt: A friend texted this while waiting for movers on moving day. Tap a line if something doesn't add up, or call it clean.

segments.label: The break
segments.text: Freight elevator broke mid-move, so the movers had to carry the sofa up the stairs from the 1st floor.

segments.label: Check-in
segments.text: Just texted that they hit the 4th floor after 6 minutes — steady pace, no breaks.

segments.label: The ETA
segments.text: I'm on the 8th floor, which is double 4, so they'll be at my door in another 6 minutes.

segments.label: The prep
segments.text: Going to prop the front door open right now.

conclusion: 1st to 4th took 6 minutes, and 8 is double 4, so they'll reach the 8th floor in 6 more minutes.

flaws.original: 1st to 4th is 3 flights of stairs (2 minutes a flight), while 4th to 8th is 4 more flights — so they need 8 more minutes, not 6.
flaws.corrupted: I'm on the 8th floor, which is double 4, so they'll be at my door in another 6 minutes.

diagnosis_choices.label: 1st to 4th is 3 flights (2 min each), while 4th to 8th is 4 flights — that's 8 more minutes, not 6.
4th to 8th is 5 flights because you count both the 4th and 8th landings, so it takes 10 more minutes.
At 6 minutes for 4 floors (1.5 min each), the remaining 4 floors actually take 7.5 minutes.
Movers always slow down on the upper floors, so doubling 6 minutes ignores fatigue.

fix_choices.label: Count flights, not floor numbers: 3 flights took 6 min, so 4 more flights take 8 min.
Count both landings (5 flights) and expect them in 10 more minutes.
Multiply 1.5 minutes per floor by 5 remaining landings for 7.5 minutes.
Add a 2-minute rest break on the 6th floor and expect them in 8 minutes.

flaws.explanation: 1st to 4th is 3 flights of stairs, not 4. Going from 4th to 8th is 4 more flights — 8 minutes, not 6.
flaws.why_tempting: '8 is double 4' feels instant and clean. Because the lobby is called the 1st floor instead of 0, the first half is one flight shorter than it sounds.
flaws.catch_rule: When climbing between numbered floors, subtract the floor numbers to count actual flights — never take a ratio of the floor numbers.
flaws.hint: How many flights of stairs did they actually climb to get from the 1st floor to the 4th?

practice.problem: A runner climbs from the 1st floor to the 5th floor in 40 seconds at a steady pace. How long to climb from the 1st floor to the 9th?
practice.answer: 80 seconds — 1st to 5th is 4 flights (10s each), and 1st to 9th is 8 flights.

diagnosis: Starting on the 1st floor means they had to climb a flight just to enter the lobby from street level.
A sofa takes two movers, so you have to split the 6-minute climb across two people.
If the freight elevator broke mid-move, the movers were already halfway up before starting the stairs.
Stairwells number the ground floor as 0, so calling it the 1st floor shifts every floor label.
fix: Include the street-to-lobby steps before calculating their pace per flight.
Check whether they started from the garage level below the 1st floor.
Verify if the building uses 0 for ground floor so 4th is really 4 flights.
Wait for the freight elevator repair instead of estimating stair pace.

diagnosis: 6 minutes to reach the 4th floor is 1.5 minutes per floor, which doesn't divide evenly into whole seconds.
Saying 'no breaks' ignores that turning a sofa around each landing adds extra time per floor.
If they hit the 4th floor after 6 minutes, they're halfway to the 8th floor, so 6 minutes is only valid if they don't pause.
You can't extrapolate a steady pace from just one checkpoint at the 4th floor.
fix: Wait for a second checkpoint on the 5th floor before estimating the ETA.
Add 30 seconds per landing turn to the 1.5-minute-per-floor pace.
Ask the movers how many breaks they plan to take before the 8th floor.
Compute 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 minutes per floor explicitly so the pace is clear.

diagnosis: Propping the door open 6 minutes early breaks building fire code even if the ETA were right.
You're propping the door 2 minutes too late because they're actually only 4 minutes away.
Propping the door now leaves it open for 12 minutes, because they still have to climb all 8 floors.
You should wait until they text from the 7th floor instead of relying on a 6-minute estimate.
fix: Wait until they're on the 7th floor before propping the door.
Prop the door now — they'll be there in 4 minutes, not 6.
Prop the door in 6 minutes since they have 12 minutes left.
Go down to the 4th floor to help them carry the last stretch.
